turns.teacher: Bilkul, Myra—shape same rehta hai, sirf uski position badalti hai. Grid par ek square ghumakar dekho: corners kahan jaayenge?

ask.text: I make an L shape on the grid using 4 squares. Now I turn the paper around. Guess: how many squares will the L have now?

child.say: 4... paper ghoomne se thodi na badalta hai. jaise mera doodle copy ghooma toh bhi wahi tha.
child.private: wo puch rahi hai paper ghumane ke baad kitne squares — ghoomne se size nahi badalta, maine bataya tha, lekin thoda doubt hai kyunki kal draw kiya tha aur teacher ne kuch aur hi bola tha.
child.sent: 4... paper ghoomne se thodi na badalta hai. jaise mera doodle copy ghooma toh bhi wahi tha.

turns.teacher: Yes, tum got it: the L still has four squares after a turn, just like your doodle. Now try a trickier one. A strip of three squares lies flat, and another stands up. Are they the same shape and size, or different?

child.private: I think it's the same because the number of shapes didn't change, just like with the paper.
child.sent: same na? teen squares teen squares hi hote hain. bas ek leta hai ek khada hai.

turns.teacher: Tum are noticing that both strips have three squares, with one lying flat and one standing up. Let’s try a notice that turns on a grid. It is two squares wide and five squares tall. After a quarter-turn, is it five wide and two tall, or five wide and three tall?

ask.text: A school notice is drawn as a rectangle 2 grid squares wide and 5 squares tall. It is turned a quarter-turn. Is it now 5 squares wide and 2 tall, or 5 wide and 3 tall?

screen.ask: A school notice is drawn as a rectangle 2 grid squares wide and 5 squares tall. It is turned a quarter-turn. Is it now 5 squares wide and 2 tall, or 5 wide and 3 tall?

child.private: skill 2 is partly understood, so I noticed the swap but doubt my answer because I count dots, not spaces. I count the dots along the edge: it has 3 dots one way and 6 the other, so the '5 and 2' feels wrong.
child.sent: 5 wide 2 tall... haan kyunki ye ulta ho jaata hai jaise main let ti hoon toh chaudi kam lambi zyada aur ulta... arrey mummy bulati hai, ek minute. pata nahi, shayad 5 and 3 bolti hoon?

turns.teacher: Tum first said five wide and two tall, then wondered about five and three. Turning the notice cannot add squares: two by five has ten, but five by three has fifteen. Go to mummy; we can pause here.

child.private: confused by teacher's numbers but just wants to stop now

end.summary: Practised recognising that moved or turned shapes stay the same shape and size.
end.parentNote: Myra practised comparing shapes on a grid after turning or moving them. They explained that the shape stays the same, using a turning cycle and a doodle as examples. There was a brief mix-up between 5×2 and 5×3; they corrected it to 10 later. At home, ask Myra to turn a small paper shape and describe what stays the same.
